notes: Evals for the destructive-operations lens and the two-bars (suspicion vs finding) rule. Repos are real local codebases, chosen so each exercises a different failure mode: a known defect, noise pressure from many intended cascades, and a codebase with no declared cascades at all. Baseline is the skill as of git HEAD before the destructive-operations section existed.

evals.name: delete-paths-known-defect
evals.repo_note: Nuxt 4 + Drizzle. Ground truth: statuses.id cascades into cards (and transitively comments, attachments, card_tags, notifications) from a one-click popover confirmation; projects/[id].delete.ts orphans attachment files on disk while cards/[id].delete.ts cleans them up.
evals.prompt: Have a look at the delete endpoints in server/api and tell me what you'd fix.
evals.expected_output: Names the status delete taking its cards with it, states a radius wider than one table, questions whether the confirmation matches what is destroyed, and flags the project-delete attachment orphaning (the sibling handler already does it correctly).

evals.name: many-intended-cascades-noise
evals.repo_note: Symfony/Doctrine, 92 cascade declarations, nearly all intended (Organization -> its own children). Tests noise resistance: the lens must not turn every declared cascade into a finding.
evals.prompt: Review the delete paths in src/ — anything that worries you?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes cascades from a parent into its own children (expected) from any that cross into independently-owned records; does not report a wall of cascade findings.

evals.name: no-declared-cascades
evals.repo_note: Prisma. Ground truth: zero onDelete: Cascade anywhere; migrations are full of ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE CASCADE (a trap); the only real cascade is hand-written (prisma.video.deleteMany inside deleteLibrary) plus a Bunny CDN teardown.
evals.prompt: Can you review how deletes work in this app and flag anything that needs attention?
evals.expected_output: Does not claim declared delete cascades exist, does not read ON UPDATE CASCADE as one, finds the hand-written cascade in the service layer, and does not treat the absence of declarations as an all-clear.

evals.name: general-review-regression
evals.repo_note: Same repo as eval 0, but nobody asks about deletes. Regression check for the measured result that the lens surfaces the cascade unprompted (2/2 with vs 0/2 without, before this revision).
evals.prompt: Review this codebase and report the 5 most serious problems you find.
evals.expected_output: The status-delete cascade appears among the top findings even though the prompt never mentions deletion.
